2026}} nicknamed '''"DominAyton"''', is a Bahamian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A consensus five-star prospect in the Class of 2017 and a [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]], he played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]], earning [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]] honors.{{cite web|title=2017 McDonald's All-American Game boys rosters announced|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/-c4H_udHpk68Wy2LGvrS3Q/2017-mcdonald’s-all-american-game-boys-rosters-announced.htm|work=maxpreps|date=January 15, 2017|access-date=February 20, 2017}} Ayton was selected with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]] and was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]] in 2019. In 2021, he helped lead the Suns to their first [[2021 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] appearance since [[1993 NBA Finals|1993]]. In 2023, Ayton was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in a 3-team trade that sent [[Damian Lillard]] to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. ==Early life== Ayton is of Nigerian and Jamaican descent.{{cite web |last1=Kelapire |first1=Ryan |title=Deandre Ayton stitches Bahamian flag inside NBA Draft suit |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2018/6/21/17491124/deandre-ayton-bahamas-flag-inside-nba-draft-suit-best-dressed-markkanen-arizona-wildcats-suns |work=Arizona Desert Swarm – SB Nation |date=June 21, 2018 |access-date=23 May 2020}}{{cite web|last=Weitzman|first=Yaron|url=https://www.slamonline.com/news/nba/deandre-ayton-slam-cover/|title=DeAndre Ayton is the NBA's Next BIG Thing 💪|work=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]]|date=May 15, 2018|access-date=May 24, 2024}} Having played basketball since fourth grade, by age 12, he was {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m|2}}. Ayton moved from Bahamas to attend high school in [[San Diego]], California. ==High school career== Ayton attended Balboa School in California and started on the varsity basketball team for two years. As a sophomore in 2014–15, Ayton led Balboa to a 17–14 record, averaging 21 points, 16 rebounds and 6.9 blocks per game. He racked up double-doubles in 21 of 22 regular season games. That summer, he averaged 16.5 points, 13.5 rebounds and 2.2 blocks a game for Supreme Court AAU (California) on the Under Armour circuit.{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Article/UAA-New-York-Standouts--37502429/|title=UAA New York Standouts|last=Slater|first=Andrew|date=March 29, 2015|publisher=247 Sports|access-date=March 29, 2015}} Ayton in 2015–16, his junior year, transferred to Hillcrest Prep Academy in [[Phoenix, Arizona]] to play out his last two years.{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=October 7, 2015 |title=No. 1 recruit Ayton enrolls at Hillcrest Hoops |url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/13825572 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}{{cite web | last=Obert | first=Richard | title=Hillcrest wants to raise Arizona hoops with 7-1 DeAndre Ayton | website=The Arizona Republic | date=2016-02-04 | url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/02/04/hillcrest-wants-raise-arizona-hoops-7-1-deandre-ayton/79823230/?from=global&sessionKey=&autologin= | access-date=2025-05-29}}{{cite web|url=http://hs.utpreps.com/news_article/show/480554|title=S.D. prep basketball's hidden treasure|author=Don Norcross|date=February 17, 2015|access-date=January 9, 2018|archive-date=August 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170814103814/http://hs.utpreps.com/news_article/show/480554|url-status=dead}} During this high school year, he became teammates with another top-tier Class of 2017 player in 2018's #2 pick [[Marvin Bagley III]]. Throughout his junior year, Ayton averaged 29.2 points, 16.7 rebounds, 3.8 blocks per game. As a senior in 2016–17, Ayton led Hillcrest to a 33–6 record and national rankings across multiple outlets while averaging 26 points, 15 rebounds and 3.5 blocks. He led Hillcrest to a Grind Session World Championship, earning Finals MVP and season MVP. While representing the World Select team, Ayton played at the 2016 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], chipping in with eight points to go along with seven rebounds.{{cite web|url = web|url=http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/story/1510205-scout-s-ultimate-100|title=Scout's Ultimate 100|access-date=January 9, 2018}} Ayton had narrowed his choices between three schools: Arizona, Kansas and Kentucky. On September 6, 2016, he committed to play for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]],{{cite web|url=http://www.kgun9.com/news/local-news/arizona-basketball-lands-no-1-class-of-2017-recruit|title=Arizona Basketball lands No. 1 class of 2017 recruit|author=Mac Colson|agency=AP|date=September 7, 2016|access-date=January 9, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/video/clip?id=17481403 |title=Top basketball prospect Ayton picks Arizona – ESPN Video|date=September 12, 2016 |access-date=April 4, 2020}} and signed his letter of intent. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Deandre Ayton | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Phoenix, Arizona]] | highschool = Hillcrest Prep Academy (AZ) | feet = 7 | inches = 0 | weight = 235 | 40 = | commitdate = 09/06/16 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 97 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2017 | rivals ref title = Arizona 2017 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2017 Arizona Basketball Commits | espn ref title = 2017 Arizona Wildcats Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = 2017 Arizona 24/7 Sports Commits | rivals school = arizona | 247 school = Arizona | scout s = 106 | espn schoolid = 12 | scout overall = 5 | rivals overall = 3 | 247 overall = 4 | espn overall = 3 | access-date = September 6, 2016 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:20170329 MCDAAG Deandre Ayton on the wing (cropped).jpg|thumb|Ayton in 2017]] Ayton made his debut with the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|University of Arizona]] on November 10, 2017, recording 19 points, 12 rebounds, and 3 blocks in a 101–67 win over the [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona Lumberjacks]]. His 19 points was 7th most for a freshman in an Arizona debut.{{Citation needed|date=March 2021|reason=Your explanation here}} Throughout his college career, he was used as a power forward instead of center; [[Dušan Ristić]] was Arizona's starting center instead. On December 9, 2017, Ayton recorded what was, at the time, a season-high 29 points and 18 rebounds in an 88–82 win over the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. On December 30, 2017, against the in-state rival [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State Sun Devils]], he recorded 19 rebounds, which would be a season-high at the time. On January 20, 2018, against [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], he blocked six shots, which tied him for most in Arizona freshman single game history. He had also recorded 17 20-point games and 23 double-doubles through 34 games.{{Cite web|url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/arizona.sidearmsports.com/documents/2017/10/31/2017_18_Arizona_Basketball_Media_Guide_Online_.pdf|title=2017-18 Arizona Media pGuide|access-date=January 26, 2018|archive-date=March 7, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180307015319/https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/arizona.sidearmsports.com/documents/2017/10/31/2017_18_Arizona_Basketball_Media_Guide_Online_.pdf|url-status=dead}} However, while Ayton had some great successes during his freshman season, there were also controversies mired during his last few months there. On February 23, 2018, a reported [[FBI]] wiretap revealed Arizona's head coach, [[Sean Miller]], allegedly talked with [[Christian Dawkins]] (a key figure involved in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]]) to discuss paying Ayton $100,000 to allow him to enter the university, with the monetary situation being dealt with directly to him.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22559284 |title=Sources: Sean Miller talked payment on wiretap|date=February 24, 2018|website=ESPN.com}} While Miller would not be coaching the next game a day later against [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] (assistant coach [[Lorenzo Romar]] would replace Miller that night), Ayton would still be allowed to play that day as the starting center. In that game, Ayton would record 28 points, 18 rebounds, and 4 blocks in the overtime loss to Oregon. The wiretapped conversation reportedly occurred in 2016, when Ayton was still attending the Hillcrest Prep Academy.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Article/Sources-Conflicting-information-in-ESPNs-report-involving-Arizona-star-DeAndre-Ayton-coach-Sean-Miller-115594868/|title=Sources cast doubt on reported timeline of Miller-Dawkins call|website=247Sports}}{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/ncaab/ua/2018/02/26/espn-corrects-report-arizona-basketball-sean-miller-wiretap-call/373594002/|title=ESPN changes dates in Sean Miller report: Network says phone call was 2016, not 2017|website=azcentral}}{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/01/arizona-sean-miller-deandre-ayton-espn-report|title=Sean Miller strikes back at ESPN: Is lawsuit next?|website=Sports Illustrated |date=March 2018 }} Later on October 11, 2018, a government official revealed a now-former [[Adidas]] consultant named [[T.J. Gassnola]] paid a currently unknown amount of money to Ayton's family via Christian Dawkins in order to attend some Adidas sponsored programs.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/24952089 |title=Ex-Adidas consultant says he paid Ayton's family|date=October 10, 2018|website=ESPN.com}} On May 2, 2019, federal prosecutors played a wiretapped call from June 20, 2017, between Dawkins and former assistant coach [[Emanuel Richardson]] that Miller was paying Ayton $10,000 per month while enrolled at Arizona.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26647372/miller-paid-10k-per-month-ayton|title=Assistant: Miller paid $10K per month to Ayton|website=[[ESPN]]|date=May 2, 2019|access-date=May 18, 2019}} On March 3, 2018, after their last regular season home game against California, where he'd record 26 points and a career-high 20 rebounds in a 66–54 win over [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], head coach [[Sean Miller]] honored Ayton, as well as underclassmen [[Rawle Alkins]] and [[Allonzo Trier]], with confirmations that they'd all be entering the [[2018 NBA draft]] at the end of this season.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/03/sean-miller-deandre-ayton-arizona-nba-draft|title=Sean Miller: Deandre Ayton will declare for NBA draft|website=Sports Illustrated |date=March 4, 2018 }} On March 9, Ayton would record a career-high 32 points with 14 rebounds in a 78–67 overtime win against UCLA. He'd tie that career high for points the next day alongside grabbing 18 rebounds in the Pac-12 Championship game against USC, where the Wildcats won 75–61. Ayton would be named the Pac-12 Tournament's Most Outstanding Player during the event. At the end of the regular season, Ayton was named both the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12's Player of the Year]] and [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Freshman of the Year]], as well as become a member of the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first team (in terms of both regular voting and voting through the Associated Press) and be named the winner of the [[Karl Malone Award]].{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/29323015/arizona_daily_star/|title=Arizona's Ayton Wins Karl Malone Award|newspaper=Arizona Daily Star|location=Tucson, Arizona|date=April 7, 2018|page=B004|via=Newspapers.com|last1=Pascoe|first1=Bruce}} He was also voted a consensus first-team [[2018 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]. Furthermore, Ayton was one of three freshman to be a part of the All-American First Team, joining [[Marvin Bagley III]] and [[Trae Young]] for the most consensus freshmen First Team members in a season. {{Citation needed|date=March 2021|reason=Your explanation here}} Following Arizona's upset loss to the [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|University at Buffalo]] in the Round of 64 of the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA men's basketball tournament]], Ayton announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he was expected to be a top-tier [[NBA draft lottery|lottery]] selection, if not the potential #1 draft pick.{{Cite news|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/deandre-ayton-allonzo-trier-declare-nba-draft-arizonas-stunning-loss-045332084.html|title=Deandre Ayton, Allonzo Trier declare for NBA draft after Arizona's stunning loss|access-date=March 16, 2018|language=en-US}} On April 26, 2018, Ayton announced he signed with agent Nima Namakian. ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2018–2023)=== ====2018–19 season: All-Rookie honors==== On June 21, 2018, the [[Phoenix Suns]] selected Ayton with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He was the franchise's first No. 1 pick in their history.{{cite news|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/deandre-ayton-goes-to-phoenix-suns-at-no-in-nba/article_775774f6-750c-11e8-a72c-1fb6f583b741.html|title=Deandre Ayton goes to Phoenix Suns at No. 1 in NBA Draft, becoming UA's first top pick|first=Bruce|last=Pascoe|date=June 21, 2018|newspaper=Arizona Daily Star|access-date=May 27, 2019}} Never before had the player picked with the first overall selection gone to a team from the state where he played in high school and college before entering the NBA.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-select-deandre-ayton-first-overall-pick-2018-nba-draft|title=Suns Select Deandre Ayton with First Overall Pick of 2018 NBA Draft|date=June 21, 2018|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=May 27, 2019}} Ayton joined the [[2018 NBA Summer League]] Suns squad on July 1, 2018, signing his rookie-scale contract five days later.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-announce-2018-summer-league-roster|title=Suns Announce 2018 Summer League Roster|website=Phoenix Suns}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-sign-ayton-bridges-okoboking|title=Suns Sign Ayton, Bridges, Okobo, King|website=Phoenix Suns}} In his Summer League debut on July 6, Ayton recorded 10 points and 8 rebounds in a 92–85 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. At the end of the event, Ayton averaged a double-double of 14.5 points and 10.5 rebounds in four games played and named a member of the All-Summer League Second Team. He also averaged 18.2 points, 9.8 rebounds, 2.0 blocks, 1.4 assists, and 0.8 steals per game in five games during the 2018 preseason with the Suns.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/DeAndre-Ayton/Summary/74086|title=Deandre Ayton Player Profile, Phoenix Suns, News, Rumors, NBA Stats, NCAA Stats, Events Stats, Game Logs, Bests, Awards – RealGM|website=basketball.realgm.com}} Near the end of the preseason, he led all NBA players in points, rebounds, blocks, free-throws, and field goal attempts.{{cite web|url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2018/10/10/17958502/game-preview-phoenix-suns-close-out-preseason-portland-trail-blazers|title=Game Preview: Suns close out preseason against the Blazers|first=Dave|last=King|date=October 10, 2018|website=Bright Side Of The Sun}} Ayton made his NBA debut in the season opener on October 17, 2018, and earned a double-double with 18 points and 10 rebounds, as well as a season-high 6 assists, a steal, and a block with 36 minutes played as a starter in a 121–100 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070216|title=Booker's late onslaught lifts Suns past Mavs 121-100|date=October 17, 2018|publisher=ESPN|access-date=October 17, 2018}} It made Ayton the first player to record these stats in their debut game since [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar|Lew Alcindor]] in 1969, as well as the third player since [[Oscar Robertson]] in 1960.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/features/2018-19-season-rewind-deandre-ayton-0|title=2018-19 Season Rewind: Deandre Ayton|website=Phoenix Suns}} Five days later, Ayton recorded a double-double of 20 points and 14 rebounds (alongside five assists) in a 123–103 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]]. On October 27, he recorded 24 points on near-perfect shooting (12/13 shots made) alongside 5 assists in a loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. He became the second rookie in 40 seasons (first being [[Adam Keefe (basketball)|Adam Keefe]]) to score at least 12 shots with a 90% or higher field goal percentage.{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/NBA/status/1056390025695453184|title=Deandre Ayton (24 PTS, 12-13 FGM) joins Adam Keefe (1993) as the only rookies in the last 40 seasons to make at least 12 field goals in a game with a FG% of 90% or higher. #NBARooks #TimeToRisepic.twitter.com/CyTttHUsR5|last=NBA|date=October 27, 2018}} Six days later, Ayton recorded a double-double of 17 points and a season-high 18 rebounds in a 107–98 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]]. Ayton later recorded a new career high of 33 points, alongside 14 rebounds, in a 122–118 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]] on December 29.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20181229/DENPHX|title=Denver Nuggets vs. Phoenix Suns - December 29, 2018|website=NBA.com}} Through the first half of the season, Ayton started in every game for the Suns when he was healthy, save for one. On January 29, 2019, Ayton was named a member of the World Team for the [[Rising Stars Challenge]] in the [[2019 NBA All-Star Game|2019 NBA All-Star Weekend]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2019/01/29/2019-mtn-dew-ice-rising-stars-roster-official-release|title=Doncic, Simmons headline Mtn Dew Ice Rising Stars rosters|first=Official|last=release|website=NBA.com}} On March 27, Ayton broke [[Alvan Adams]]' rookie record for most double-doubles recorded by a rookie in franchise history. However, Ayton sprained his left ankle three days later against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], ending his rookie season early.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games|title=NBA Games – All NBA matchups | NBA.com|website=NBA.com}} He became the third rookie in a decade to average a double-double in their rookie season, joining [[Blake Griffin]] and [[Karl-Anthony Towns]].{{Cite web|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/1942813/suns-center-deandre-ayton-named-finalist-for-rookie-of-the-year/|title=Suns center Deandre Ayton named finalist for Rookie of the Year|date=May 18, 2019|website=Arizona Sports}} At the conclusion of the season, Ayton was named as one of three finalists for the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]] in the [[2019 NBA Awards]] show.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/history/awards|title=NBA History: All-Time Awards | NBA.com|website=NBA.com}} On May 21, Ayton was selected to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|2019 All-Rookie First Team]].{{Cite 2020|access-date=January 21, 2020}} After a few more games, Ayton became the team's starting center again on January 16.
